note: refactor-cpu-core phase 2. The whole-chip numbers T4/T5/T8 ask for do NOT exist: the design cannot be placed, because its 64 KB main memory is modelled as an on-chip array (rtl/ram_async.sv) with no memory abstraction behind it. See docs/cpu-core.md.

target.target_freq_status: aspirational: rtl/pll.v is generated for 50 MHz but rtl/top.sv never instantiates it, so the board runs the raw 25 MHz pin

whole_chip.reason: ram_async #(.A(16)) infers a 64 KB on-chip memory; hx8k has 32 x 4 kbit BRAM = 16 KB total. yosys cannot map it, falls back to logic and emits 1,727,271 AND gates / 4,954,853 wires, then never finishes ABC9.

core_only.harness: rtl/cpu_fmax_top.sv: one core plus a 2 KB synchronous-read RAM with ram_async's timing. No memory arbiter, so a difference between runs is a difference between cores.

arlet.critical_path: starts at a registered decode signal (V) -> store -> write_back -> inc -> index_y -> dst_reg -> regfile -> ALU half-carry -> PC. 11.75 ns logic.

v2.critical_path: starts at the BRAM read data: RDATA -> di -> combinational decode (ir) -> flag/ALU select -> store data -> carry chain -> C flag. 14.12 ns logic.

throughput.note: static mean CPI over Breakout's 1,928 instructions, from docs/cpu-timing-*.json

other_clock_consumers.psg: rate derived from the CLK_HZ parameter (chip.sv:22, top.sv:22); clock-portable, no benefit
other_clock_consumers.lcd_serialiser: runs at the system clock, so a faster clock is a shorter frame push - the one part that gains
other_clock_consumers.compositor: per-line cycle budget scales with the clock

psg_register_reads.evidence: rtl/psg.sv CPU-interface block only assigns dout; no register read alters sequencer or channel state. So the corpus's one indexed MMIO site (sta PSG_CH,y at src/main.asm:2479) is safe against a spurious read.
